hot_themes: The psychology of money and love
hook_patterns: Direct address calling out a specific modern identity (e.g., 'You are a Gen Z working 9-5')
Contrarian or provocative statement challenging a common belief (e.g., 'Money can't buy love')
Hyper-specific relatable scenario with an exaggerated emotional reaction
ideas_for_us: Best Friend 1 thinks they are indispensable at work; Best Friend 2 explains the 'Dunning-Kruger effect' and why they are actually easily replaceable, using a humorous 'cloning' animation.

A skit where Best Friend 1 tries to impress a date with expensive gifts; Best Friend 2 explains 'Limerence' and why the date only likes the gifts, not the person, using visual metaphors of receipt holders.
Best Friend 1 is spiraling over a minor text message delay; Best Friend 2 explains 'Cognitive Distortion' and 'Mind Reading' by visualizing the brain as a toxic overthinker character.

Best Friend 1 quits their passion project to make money but feels empty; Best Friend 2 explains the 'Endowment Effect' and 'Intrinsic vs. Extrinsic Motivation' by showing the hobby literally turning into a grey, boring robot.
